rows.title: Compromise would save Lamont from veto override on funding fight
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont and legislative leaders said they agreed on a deal to deliver $40 million for special education and $2.88 million in grants.

rows.title: Lamont, officials brace for federal cuts to Medicaid
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont warned on Thursday that the likely impact in CT of all cuts Congress could make to Medicaid would be a fiscal nightmare.

rows.title: Lamont cuts spending at CT public colleges, other agencies
rows.standfirst: One week after agreeing to bolster grants for special education, Gov. Ned Lamont slashed $41 million in other spending on Friday.

rows.title: Will federal budget cuts sink CT tax break for families?
rows.standfirst: Advocates say tax relief such as a child tax credit is needed now as support programs shrink, but federal cuts could complicate matters.

rows.title: CT cities and towns urge lawmakers to battle Lamont
rows.standfirst: The Connecticut Conference of Municipalities launched a campaign attacking the governor for allowing CT’s overreliance on property taxes.

rows.title: Lamont’s budget for CT is $230 million short
rows.standfirst: Employee health care costs would push Gov. Ned Lamont’s spending plan more than $100 million over the spending cap in the next fiscal year.

rows.title: CSCU saved hundreds of millions while asking for more
rows.standfirst: CT’s public colleges and universities pushed hard for funds since COVID rocked their finances. But now, they have more than $1 billion saved.

rows.title: Have CT towns benefited under Lamont? Depends on whom you ask
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont said communities have benefited greatly under his leadership. The lobbying group for municipalities disagrees.

rows.title: CT loses $155M in federal aid for public health programs
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration nixed about $155M in grants that support infectious disease management, genetic screening of newborns and more.

rows.title: Debate over CT pension calculations heats up
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers are weighing whether overtime earnings should continue to be factored in when calculating retirement pay for state employees.

rows.title: CT leaders say they’ll counter swiftly if Trump cuts more federal aid
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont and legislative leaders said on Friday CT’s piggy banks are large, and the state won’t hesitate to crack them.

rows.title: Trump freezes $14 million in aid for K-12 education in CT
rows.standfirst: Connecticut education officials still were working early Monday to identify all frozen funds and affected school districts.

rows.title: Nursing home workers to remind CT officials a strike is possible
rows.standfirst: SEIU District 1199 New England will announce Tuesday that a preliminary-yet-necessary procedural step toward a strike was taken this week.
